data.name: Kelton
data.gender_notes: Kelton is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kelton is an Old English name, derived from the word 'cealtun'. It originally meant 'enclosure' or 'young horse'. Over time, it came to be associated with the idea of protection, as a young horse requires care and shelter to grow into strength. The name Kelton carries the meaning “Young horse enclosure” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kelton usually hope their child will grow to embody young horse enclosure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes protection, care, and growth.
data.etymology: Kelton belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young horse enclosure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kelton total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: קלטון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קלטון מקורו במילה העברית 'קלט', שפירושה 'מקום של קלט' או 'אסיף'. שם זה נמצא בשימוש במסורת הנוצרית ככינוי למקום או לאזור.

in_greek.name: Κέλτον
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Κέλτον προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'Κέλτ', που σημαίνει 'τόπος του Κέλτ' ή 'γη των Κελτών'. Στην παράδοση της πρώιμης Εκκλησίας, το όνομα αυτό μπορεί να σχετίζεται με περιοχές που κατοικούσαν Κελτικοί λαοί.

in_latin.name: Kelton
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Kelton derivatur ex voce Latina 'Celtorum', quae significat 'locus Celtorum' vel 'terra Celtorum'. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc ad designandum locum vel regionem in qua habitabant Celtarum populi.

in_english.name: Kelton
in_english.meaning: from the spring town or the stone town
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kelton is of English and Scottish origin, derived from the Old English words 'ceol' meaning 'spring' or 'slate' and 'tun' meaning 'town' or 'settlement'. Therefore, Kelton can be interpreted as 'from the spring town' or 'the stone town'. In Christian tradition, the name Kelton may signify a place of gathering or community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kelton carries Anglo-Saxon origins and has notable connections to rural and horse-rearing traditions. Although Kelton is a lesser-known name than other Old English monikers, its cultural significance lies in its historical link to the protection, care, and nurturing of animals, particularly young horses.
data.spiritual_significance: Kelton is an evocative name from a Christian perspective. It is a reminder that those smaller, weaker, or vulnerable components of one's sphere deserve protection, shelter, and care. The spiritual significance of Kelton includes conveying a sense of responsibility for nurturing others and spreading love and protection to those around us. This interpretation highlights the belief that every individual possesses inherent value, regardless of their size, age, or strength.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kelton: Celestial warrior, bringing divine guidance and protection. Derived from the Celtic name Caelan, meaning 'slender' or 'handsome stranger from the far-off hills'.

historical_references.reference: St Kelton, a Welsh saint. He was a disciple of Saint David and is believed to have established a monastery in what is now County Kildare, Ireland, around 500 AD. Kelton is mentioned in the Welsh Triads as one of the 'Three Saints of the Forest of Dean'.
historical_references.context: Early Christian period; Wales and Ireland

historical_references.reference: Kelton Church, also known as St Kelton's Church, is a small 13th century parish church located in the village of the same name in Derbyshire, England. The church is believed to have been named after an early Christian hermit who lived in the area and is mentioned in historical records from the 13th and 14th centuries.
